_meta.purpose: Deciding whether a posting is remote, onsite or a project (freelance/contract) engagement — T031a.
_meta.why_this_is_config: Same reason role_families.json is config: these patterns decide which opportunities a user sees, and they must be editable and versioned without a Python change. An assessment records the config version it ran under, so a pattern added later never silently rewrites an old decision.
_meta.three_values_only: The opportunity table permits remote, onsite and project. There is deliberately no 'hybrid' value: a hybrid role requires the candidate to be physically present in the employer's city on some days, so for every downstream question that matters — cost of living, tax residence, relocation, visa — it behaves exactly like onsite. The hybrid signal is still reported in `evidence` so the distinction is not lost, it just does not get its own bucket.
_meta.unknown_stays_null: A posting whose arrangement cannot be read is NULL, not onsite. Defaulting to onsite would be an invented fact about a job nobody read, and onsite is the value that drives relocation and cost-of-living arithmetic — the most expensive place to be wrong.
_meta.precedence: project beats remote beats onsite. A freelance contract delivered remotely is a project engagement first: how the person is engaged and paid changes tax, invoicing and whether there is a salary at all, and that matters more than where the work happens. `remote` is still recorded in evidence when both fire.
_meta.false_positive_note: The single biggest risk here is the word 'contract'. It is ordinary vocabulary in the domains this candidate works in — 'contract manufacturing', 'contract negotiation', 'contract management', 'under contract' — so a bare 'contract' match would misclassify a large share of genuine permanent supply-chain and manufacturing roles as freelance. Every project pattern below therefore requires the word to sit in a phrase that names the ENGAGEMENT, never the word alone.

project.label: Project / freelance engagement
project.structured_note: Matched against a source's OWN employment-type field where it publishes one (Arbeitnow's `job_types`, a board's `employment_type`). A structured field is a statement by the employer and is far safer than reading prose, so it is checked first.

remote.label: Remote
remote.negation_note: An explicit refusal beats a mention, the same rule detect_visa_signal uses. A posting that says 'this role is not remote' contains the word 'remote' and must not be filed as one.

onsite.label: On site
onsite.hybrid_note: A hybrid match resolves to onsite, for the reason in _meta.three_values_only, and records 'hybrid' in its evidence.
